title: Falsy `source` is handled three different ways inside _execute_lazy (raw for graph pruning, coerced to "live" for cache-key validation and checkpoint scenario) — latent inconsistency
description: _execute_lazy receives `source: str = "live"`. Graph preparation / live-switch pruning uses the RAW value (`_prepare_graph_with_edges(graph, target_node_id, source=source)` at lines 709-713, which flows into `projection_planner.prune_live_switch_edges` where `source not in input_scenario_map.values()` and `mapped != source` compare against the raw string). However, two other sites in the SAME function silently coerce a falsy source to "live": the dataframe-cache-key source check computes `effective_source = source or "live"` (line 807) and validates `cache_key.source != effective_source`, and the checkpoint-decision scenario passes `node_source_overrides.get(nid, source or "live")` (line 1360). Node builders, meanwhile, receive the raw `source` (via `_build_funcs` `node_source_overrides.get(nid, source)`). If a caller ever passes `source=""` (or any falsy string), the graph would be pruned and node functions built under `""`, while cache admission and checkpoint MODEL_SCORE-skip logic would behave as if `"live"` — three divergent interpretations of one argument. This is a contract inconsistency, not a crash.
evidence: Line 709-713 `_prepare_graph_with_edges(graph, target_node_id, source=source)` → projection.py prune_live_switch_edges compares raw `source`. Line 807 `effective_source = source or "live"` then `if cache_key.source != effective_source: raise`. Line 1360 `_checkpoint_decision(..., node_source_overrides.get(nid, source or "live"))`; _checkpoint_decision (line 440) skips MODEL_SCORE only when `scenario != "live"`. Line 1484 in _build_funcs uses `node_source_overrides.get(nid, source)` (raw). The presence of the defensive `source or "live"` coercion at exactly two of the three sites shows a falsy source was anticipated but not handled uniformly.
